text:
alex: FYI I'm starting the shepherd for tonight's change window at 21:00 UTC — cross-service deploy (API, runtime, router, console). tagging owners. :wave:
marie: thanks alex. what's the plan for version pinning? we need to avoid auto-latest on the router.
kevin: router will be pinned to v2.1.3 for the window. console is on v1.14.0 canary, will hold at 5% unless we get green signals.
sophia: runtime will land quant-kernel toggles in v1.8.2. note: kv-eviction config change is behind flag, won't roll out yet.
alex: deploy-bot, please create the staged waves and prevent automatic next-wave kick if any canary alert fires.
deploy-bot: @channel Creating release shepherd: wave-0 (canary) -> Router v2.1.3, Runtime v1.8.2-canary, API v3.0.7-canary. Canary duration: 20m. Auto-advance: OFF.
nate: rollback criteria proposed: >1% error rate or p95 latency increase > 200ms sustained for 5m. also any functional 5xx spike in API endpoints invalidates the canary.
marie: +1 to the criteria. add a health-check on /v1/health that checks model-serving kv hit-ratio as well.
sre-bot: Runbook link: https://internal.redwood/runbooks/deploy-shepherd. If rollback triggered: runbook -> tag and pin previous stable variants, route 100% back, and notify paging.
kevin: console QA: we have one schema change in telemetry that could cause non-fatal log spam. it's allowed, but set log level to WARN for the window. I'll push a runtime config change afterwards.
sophia: quick config snippet for pin config: ```
service_pins:
  router: "v2.1.3"
  runtime: "v1.8.2-canary"
  api: "v3.0.7-canary"
  console: "v1.14.0-canary-5pct"
```
alex: release notes draft: https://docs.internal/release-notes/3955006789. callout: improved batching kernels, router conn pooling tweak, console telemetry schema - opt-in.
marie: are DB migrations required?
kevin: no DB migrations. minor API contract bump uses optional fields only. clients should be fine.
sophia: observability hooks: adding traces for kv access and kernel selection. please ensure sample rate is low for the canary to avoid noise (0.01).
alex: any blockers?
nate: load test on staging looked fine up to 2x expected traffic. small spike in tail latency for long-seq requests but within rollback thresholds.
marie: ok let's proceed. alex — i'll be on call for the first 45m of the window.
alex: starting wave-0 now. deploy-bot, kick it.
deploy-bot: wave-0 kickoff at 3955008000. Tasks: route 5% to canary router, deploy runtime podset with canary images, register API version in gateway. Will post updates.
sre-bot: Monitoring dashboards: ENG-Runtime / ENG-Router / ENG-API links posted to #oncall. Alerting thresholds set as discussed.
deploy-bot: wave-0 progress: router: DONE, runtime: DONE, api: DONE. health-check pass at 21:08 UTC.
kevin: observed small log spam in console telemetry, changed level to WARN. no impact.
sophia: KV hit ratio stable. tracing sample rate at 0.01.
nate: canary looks green for 20m mark. no 5xx, p95 latency within baseline.
marie: i'm doing quick UX smoke on console flows — all good.
alex: moving to wave-1 (50%). keep auto-advance OFF. manual check next.
deploy-bot: wave-1 kickoff at 3955008600. routing 50% to new stack.
sre-bot: wave-1 monitoring: slight p95 bump on long sequences; still under threshold.
nate: recommending full rollout in 30m if stable. rollback criteria still in place.
marie: leaving note in release-notes: "Canary verified. Full rollout pending final verification at +30m."
alex: thanks team. I'll keep the shepherd open until 22:30 UTC. ping me if anything regresses. :thumbsup:
